Dhammapaccanīya (2), Tikatikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (5) 11.9.
The Triplet of the Wholesome (Kusalattika), the Triplet of the Visible (Sanidassanattika)
Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor non-obscured-reactive, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor non-obscured-reactive by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor non-obscured-reactive, there arises a state that is unwholesome and non-obscured-reactive by way of root condition. [Dependent on] a state that is neither wholesome nor non-obscured-reactive...
Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor unwholesome, neither visible nor impinging, a state that is neither indeterminate nor visible nor impinging arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor unwholesome, neither visible nor impinging, states that are both neither wholesome nor unwholesome, neither visible nor impinging, and neither indeterminate nor visible nor impinging arise by way of root condition. [Dependent on] a state that is neither wholesome...

Non-reactive and non-demonstrable phenomena arise conditioned by a cause that is non-reactive and non-demonstrable.
